_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::solid_mechanics#5, and a FALSIFICATION of it. The entry claimed structural Neumann conditions need NUMDOF: 6 and that NUMDOF: 3 'silently drops the moment components'. On a 3D SOLID mesh a node carries three dofs: NUMDOF: 3 runs and exits 0; NUMDOF: 6 with the last three slots zeroed runs, exits 0 and passes the SAME result test pinned to 1e-12 (NUMDOF6_ZEROED_RESULT_FAILURES=0), so the extra slots change nothing; and NUMDOF: 6 with one moment slot switched ON aborts with 'Number of Dimensions in Neumann_Evaluation is 3. Further DoFs are not considered.' from solid_3D_ele/4C_solid_3D_ele_surface_evaluate.cpp and exit 1. Nothing is dropped silently. NUMDOF: 6 is the SHELL7P convention and NUMDOF: 9 the BEAM3R one; on SOLID it is 3. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: Number of Dimensions in Neumann_Evaluation is 3. Further DoFs are not considered.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: zero the moment slot in the third arm so it asks the continuum element only for forces. The Neumann_Evaluation abort vanishes, EXIT_NUMDOF6_MOMENT becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
